subject.title: Support Azure Foundry GPT Realtime Talk via gateway relay

question: Should OpenClaw ship Azure Foundry Realtime Talk now as an API-key-only Gateway Relay path first, or wait until Entra/managed identity and live quota proof are available?
rationale: The code boundary is clear enough to keep the issue open, but the credential model, redirect handling, GA endpoint shape, SecretRef guidance, and live-proof bar are security-sensitive product choices that automation should not settle.

options.title: Phase API-Key Gateway Relay First
options.body: Implement the current GA Azure endpoint and deployment handling behind Gateway Relay with server-side API-key/SecretRef support, constrained redirect behavior if needed, Azure diagnostics, docs, and tests; add Entra as a follow-up.

options.title: Wait For Entra And Live Quota
options.body: Keep the issue open but defer implementation until a maintainer can provision a supported Azure Realtime deployment and decide the Entra/managed identity contract up front.

options.title: Close As Out Of Scope For Core
options.body: Reject first-class Azure Realtime Talk in core and require a provider/plugin package only if maintainers decide the existing plugin API is sufficient and no bundled OpenAI provider change should own it.

recommendation.title: Phase API-Key Gateway Relay First
recommendation.body: Implement the current GA Azure endpoint and deployment handling behind Gateway Relay with server-side API-key/SecretRef support, constrained redirect behavior if needed, Azure diagnostics, docs, and tests; add Entra as a follow-up.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored the GA realtime bridge foundation and is the broadest owner signal for the OpenAI realtime/Talk implementation boundary.
